text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler ceiling reached for pool `gpu-prod-west`. Current nodes=48 (max). Queue growth observed, token-generation requests throttled. Triggered at 2025-11-19T02:10:56Z (thread root).

mel (SRE oncall): I'm on it. Seeing queue length spike on `inference-queue-usw2`. Any recent deploys? 

ram (eng-infra): No deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler logs show repeated `scale->desired == max` decisions. Policy is max_nodes=48, scale_step=8, cooldown=5m.

lee (eng-runtime): CPU on the scheduler is fine, but GPU node utilization is ~92%. KV cache hit rate is low for this workload so more tokens hitting runtime. We're hitting pod density limits on the pool (k8s max pods per node).

mel (SRE oncall): Customer impact? Jordan?

jordan (product): Product metrics: 12% of live requests are delayed beyond 2s tail latency; two enterprise customers seeing >5% error-level throttles (HTTP 429). CS pinged.

tanya (customer-success): Confirmed: AcmeCorp reported timeouts for heavy batch rerank calls ~02:09Z. They're on Dedicated capacity but route through shared GPU pool for burst.

aaron (support): Logged ticket INC-9834 and notified account team.

mel (SRE oncall): Initial mitigation options: 1) temporary manual cap raise of gpu-prod-west to 64 nodes, 2) apply temporary global request shedding for non-SLA customers, 3) increase pod density by switching to larger instance type (longer). Recommend manual cap raise + shedding for lowest priority classes.

lee (eng-runtime): I can enable request-priority-based shedding quickly via the runtime flags. Patch below: 

```
# enable shedding for priority < 20
redwood runtime config set --pool gpu-prod-west --shed-low-priority true --shed-threshold 0.8
```

mel (SRE oncall): I'll request manual cap bump from infra console. @ram can you pre-authorize? Need 64 nodes for ~20 minutes to clear backlog.

ram (eng-infra): I can approve. Preparing the manual override command. Will handoff to mel to execute once approved.

mel (SRE oncall): Executing manual bump now. Running admin command: 

```
# manual bump
redwood-admin scale-set --pool gpu-prod-west --max-nodes 64 --reason "incident: autoscale ceiling hit" --expires-in 30m
```

mel (SRE oncall): Command returned 202 Accepted. Autoscaler max set to 64. Kicking off scale up.

incident-bot: :information_source: Scaling event: desired=56 -> provisioning new nodes. Expected join in ~4-6m.

lee (eng-runtime): While nodes come up, toggled shedding for non-SLA. Runtime patch applied, dropping low-priority requests.

jordan (product): Noted impact: shedding will affect free-tier and background eval jobs, enterprise customers unaffected. Sending message to status page and affected customers list.

tanya (customer-success): Notifying AcmeCorp: temporary queueing may be resolved in ~10m.

mel (SRE oncall): Scale progress: 10 nodes joining, 26 still pending. Queue length decreasing slowly.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: New nodes joined: 16/56. Pod scheduler backlog decreasing.

aaron (support): AcmeCorp replied: seeing partial recovery and decreased timeouts. Thanks.

lee (eng-runtime): Observability: per-token latency back to baseline for high-priority routes. KV cache priming in progress; hit-rate improving.

mel (SRE oncall): Monitoring next 30m. After backlog cleared we should revert max-nodes to 48 and disable shedding. We'll create a short post-incident note.

ram (eng-infra): Filing follow-up: we should revisit scale policy — consider increasing default max for gpu-prod-west or enable auto-increase under emergency mode. Created infra-ticket INFRA-1229.

jordan (product): Also recommend adding a runtime guard that prefers request-level degradation (non-SLA) earlier to avoid hitting node/max.

mel (SRE oncall): Agreed. For now, manual actions mitigated customer-visible impact. I'll hand this to next oncall in 20m for watch.

incident-bot: :clipboard: Handoff: mel -> night-oncall (sam). Summary: autoscaler max hit; manual cap raise to 64 nodes applied; low-priority shedding enabled; backlog draining; monitoring.

mel (SRE oncall): Thanks team. Tagging postmortem owners: ram, lee, jordan. I'll update runbook with exact commands used. 

lee (eng-runtime): Patch to disable shedding (post-incident): 
```
redwood runtime config set --pool gpu-prod-west --shed-low-priority false
```

mel (SRE oncall): Final note: leave alert thresholds as-is but add a secondary alert when scale decisions repeatedly hit max for >3 cycles.

incident-bot: :tada: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
